items.note: Quoted from villageinfo: geographical area 1966 hectares, total population 6,383, about 1,247 houses.
Most temples in Udaypur are built of red sandstone in open space and placed on a raised plinth.
A major portion of the wall is in fair condition with some collapsed sections in the east and northeastern parts.
A 6th century CE cave on the hill south of the village, under Forest Department ownership, southeast of the larger hill (Jind Baba ki pahadi).
A two-line inscription beside the sculpture noticed for the first time and yet to be deciphered.
Three Hindu sculptures in series and an isolated Ganesha on the hill facing Udaypur; details so deteriorated that dedication cannot be identified.
Chanderi Darwaza built in the 11th century CE in the northwest of the village, in government ownership; a trapezoidal stone gate (⚠ garbled OCR).
Raja Mahal: arched eastern entrance with decorated stone columns, projecting corner bastions with multiple arrow slits (⚠ garbled OCR).
Barah Khambi: 11th century CE as recorded by stone signage near the structure; 12 pillared halls on a high raised stone platform.
Barah Khambi is a centrally protected monument in good shape; an inscription of Samvat 1625 on a pillar is of a later period.
Octagonal chhatri near Uday-sagar on the outskirts of Bada Talab, with carved columns; undated.
Ram Janki Mandir: decorated stair leads to a pillared mandapa; construction style similar to the palace, implying 13th century CE.
Garbhagriha houses idols of Rama, Lakshmana and Sita; mandapa walls painted red and gold; temple needs sensitive conservation.
